title: Honest Intervals for Indirect Effects in Sparse Graphon Network Experiments
banked_reason: D0.5 tier=subfield below field: sound finite-sample conditional certification and same-class lower benchmark, but no matched feasible honest-length frontier; isolate indistinguishability blocks the directed lift.
gap_reasons: The note proves a same-class three-component minimax lower benchmark and a computable conditionally honest interval, but it never bounds the interval's feasible envelope by the analytic lower envelope.

The title's honest length frontier is not delivered: what is established is a conservative finite-sample procedure plus a nonmatching lower benchmark for a distinct target on the note's maintained class.

Two supported response configurations that agree on all nonisolates and assign respectively +1 and -1 to every isolate induce exactly the same conditional observed-data law, yet their targets differ by 2B I_0(A)/n.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived exact degree-adaptive lattice-score moments and Hoeffding projections, a polynomial-time graph-adaptive PC-balanced interval with finite-sample conditional coverage, and same-class graph, interior-bump, and lattice lower benchmarks. The requested matched field-level frontier collapsed because conditional isolate indistinguishability forces a linear isolate radius, while the feasible positive-degree certificate remains too coarse; closing either gap requires a redesigned problem or new substrate.
tldr: A Bernoulli network experiment reveals a derivative only through the exact binomial support associated with each realized degree. The proposal studies the finite-population derivative \(\theta_n\) in the known-rank sparse-graphon model, uses \(h_i(h)=\max\{h,\delta_{N_i}\}\) so every positive degree has a normalized local score, and reports a graph-observable interval radius containing exact degree-level bias, exact inverse score moments, graph dependence, isolates, and feasible-PC remainders. The supported-unit benchmark has lattice, interior, and graph-floor phases. The finite-sample bridge bounds the difference from Li and Wager's finite indirect effect by the displayed degree-exact smoothness and isolate terms, and this difference is \(o_P(\sqrt{\rho_n})\) along maintained sequences in the stated sparsity regime. Li and Wager's equation~(43) is transferred only on the intersection with every source hypothesis and under \(\liminf_n\sigma_{\mathrm{IND},n}>0\); no containment of the maintained class in their theorem is asserted. Because same-class isolate testing gives only the proved \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E\sqrt{I_0(A)}\) term while the safe interval pays \(Bn^{-1}\mathbb E I_0(A)\), no sharp minimax or honest expected-length frontier is claimed, and a rate-sharp feasible PC construction at logarithmic degree remains open.
gap: Li and Wager prove asymptotic normality for a PC estimator of their finite and population indirect effects, but they do not give finite-sample honest length for the distinct realized derivative target or handle exact low-degree support. Standard honest nonparametric theory has no random exposure lattice, graph projector, or latent-type-dependent isolate tail.
fill: The project derives exact score moments at every positive degree, proves a finite-sample bridge to the published indirect effect, constructs PC-balanced observable radii, establishes supported-unit upper and lower rates plus a degree-tail modulus, and isolates the one remaining tail-adaptation question instead of asserting a false matched frontier.
